report.name: tv46l_halcon_interleaved_pcap_analysis
report.capture_notes: Manual Wireshark/Dumpcap capture (4.6.6, nanosecond resolution, no capture filter) taken 2026-08-18 ~12:38 while HALCON was configured for interleaved IR/VL data. Timestamps: capture file created 12:38:59.

verdict.one_line: THE HALCON PCAP DOES NOT CONTAIN TRUE IR/VL INTERLEAVED GVSP: it contains ZERO GVSP image blocks (no leader/data/trailer, no Mono16, no YUV422_8). HALCON's own GVCP session wrote the dual-mode register 0x10a110=2 at t=21.6128 (ACK success), then repeatedly configured/enabled the stream channel ~14 times, but the camera never delivered a single image packet.
evidence_chain: Protocol hierarchy accounts for all 1769 packets: eth 1769, lldp 10, ip 1749, udp 1749 (gvcp 1726, gvsp 22, dhcp 1), arp 10. No other IP protocol exists; there is no image traffic of any kind.

All 22 packets Wireshark dissects as 'GVSP' are proprietary FLIR keep-alive / packet-size-negotiation traffic: 18 are ASCII 'stream_keep_alive\0' from PC:64797 to the camera's current SCSP0 port; 4 are camera:36696->PC:64797 negotiation probes (payload sizes 1068/1332/1464/1472 = 1076/1340/1472/1480 UDP). None has a valid GVSP format byte.
Zero GVSP LEADER (0x01), DATA (0x02), or TRAILER (0x03) packets. Pixel formats 0x01100007 (Mono16 IR) and 0x02100032 (YUV422_8 visible) never appear.

Frame-length distribution confirms it: dominated by 54/58/60/566-byte GVCP frames; the only frames >1.1 KB are the four negotiation probes (max 1514 bytes, one frame). No 1514-byte GVSP data-packet burst and no 614400-byte image data.

HALCON's own GVCP control session (PC:64795, the same port that performed all node-map READMEM and heartbeat reads) wrote WRITEREG 0x10a110=2 at t=21.612785600 (frame 1109); camera ACKed success (frame 1110, status 0x0000). This contradicts the earlier 'HALCON resets the register to 0' finding.

After the dual-mode write HALCON re-armed the stream channel (SCDA0=0xa9fec051, SCP0=0xfd1d), read SCSP0, sent stream_keep_alive to that port, wrote 0x10a104=1 (stream enable), and ~28 ms later wrote 0x10a108=1, then cleared SCP0/SCDA0. This enable/stop cycle repeated ~14 times (t=27.97..37.19) plus one final 0x10a108=1 at t=62.955. The camera sent no image data on any cycle.
GVSP stream never delivered: zero blocks, zero frames, no FPS. HALCON is NOT receiving any GVSP stream in this capture.
verdict.answer: No. This capture shows HALCON ACTIVATING dual mode (0x10a110=2, acked) but receiving ZERO image data. The camera never streams to HALCON at all - not IR, not visible, not interleaved. This pcap cannot demonstrate HALCON receiving interleaved IR/VL GVSP because the interleaved data is not present on the wire.

question_answers.q: Does HALCON receive the TV46L native interleaved IR/VL GVSP stream?
question_answers.a: No evidence of it. The capture contains zero GVSP image blocks. HALCON's handle (PC:64795) wrote the dual-mode register and enabled the stream ~14 times, but the camera sent no image data.
No. No GVSP leader with pixel format 0x01100007; no Mono16 blocks; no 614400-byte payloads.
No. No GVSP leader with pixel format 0x02100032; no YUV422_8 blocks.

question_answers.q: Do IR and visible alternate on one stream?
question_answers.a: N/A - neither source is present, so no alternation can be observed. Frame rate is not computable (0 frames).

question_answers.q: Which register activates the dual mode, and who writes it?
question_answers.a: Register 0x10a110 = 2 is the dual-mode activation (1=IR only, 2=IR+visible). In THIS capture HALCON's own GVCP session writes it (frame 1109, port 64795) at t=21.6128 and the camera ACKs success (frame 1110). No external process writes it. This contradicts the earlier tv46l-halcon-dual-mode.md finding that HALCON resets it to 0; here HALCON writes 2 directly and it is accepted.

question_answers.q: What is the exact GVCP sequence HALCON performs?
question_answers.a: Full chronological WRITEREG table below. Summary: CCP 0x0a00=1 @16.3945; GVCP config 0x0954=0 @16.403; GVSP config 0x0960=0x40000000 (64-bit block ID) @16.4047; SCCONF0 0x0d24=0 @16.4058; SCDA0=0xa9fec051 @16.4104; SCP0=0xfd1d @16.4108; SCPS0 negotiation @16.41..17.30 (0x4000xxxx/0xC000xxxx alternating, final ~0x5DC=1500/0x5E0); teardown SCP0/SCDA0=0 @17.30; 0x10a110=2 @21.6128; re-arm SCDA0/SCP0 @21.631; 0x10a104=1 @21.6323; 0x10a108=1 @21.6605; teardown; repeated start/stop cycles @27.97..37.19; final 0x10a108=1 @62.955; CCP release @72.92.

question_answers.q: How does this compare to the ThermoView capture?
question_answers.a: Both write 0x10a110=2 and both use GVCP code 0x0082 for WRITEREG. ThermoView additionally writes 0x0938 (heartbeat), 0x0d08 SCPD0=0, and the provider/stream config 0x20a134/0x20a138/0x20a148, and it does NOT enable 64-bit block ID (0x0960). HALCON writes 0x0960=0x40000000 (64-bit block ID enabled), 0x0954=0, 0x0d24=0, and never writes 0x20a1xx registers (it only reads them). ThermoView uses SCP0=50554, HALCON SCP0=64797. The decisive difference is behavioral: ThermoView's capture contains 64,542 GVSP image frames (236 blocks); HALCON's capture contains 0.

question_answers.q: What does HALCON actually expose/return in this session?
question_answers.a: From the app-side report (scripts/tv46l_dual_mode_halcon_test.py, 11:25 run, preopen): HALCON delivers only Mono16 IR frames at ~7.5 FPS (226 IR, 0 visible) even when 0x10a110=2 is written before open. In THIS 12:38 capture HALCON itself wrote 0x10a110=2, but the wire shows zero frames of any format. STEP 11 repo search (tv46l-halcon-dual-mode.md, tv46l_dual_mode_halcon_cam_0004.json) corroborates: HALCON's FLK_TI_StreamDataSourceSelector exposes only IR_Data/VL_Data strings and never surfaces dual-source frames to the app.

question_answers.q: Why does the camera not stream to HALCON even though 0x10a110=2 is acked?
question_answers.a: Not fully determined from this pcap. Candidate causes, all consistent with the wire: (a) HALCON never writes the provider configuration 0x20a134/0x20a138/0x20a148 that ThermoView writes before dual mode; (b) HALCON enables 64-bit block ID (0x0960=0x40000000) which the camera's dual-source engine may reject while still ACKing the register write; (c) HALCON holds CCP and configures the channel in a way the camera's interleaved mode does not accept (SCPS0 ~1500 with no jumbo, no SCPD0). Any of these would explain the observed start/stop retry loop with no data.

question_answers.q: What is the recommended next experiment?
question_answers.a: Capture a ThermoView session and a HALCON session back-to-back on the same camera/link with Wireshark, and diff the EXACT WRITEREG/READREG stream (same registers in same order). Specifically: 1) record ThermoView's 0x20a134/0x20a138/0x20a148 values, 2) after writing 0x10a110=2, re-read 0x10a110 (with CCP) to confirm it stays 2, 3) test writing 0x0960=0 (32-bit block ID) on HALCON's channel before enable, 4) test writing the 0x20a1xx provider registers that ThermoView writes. Also test on HALCON whether GVSP config 64-bit block ID is required for its receive path.

gvcp_write_timeline.name: SCDA0/SCP0 set, SCSP0 read, stream_keep_alive, 0x10a104=1, 0x10a108=1, SCP0/SCDA0=0

common: Same GVCP write convention: WRITEREG = 0x0082 in this Wireshark/FLIR decoding.
Both set SCDA0=0xa9fec051 (PC) and hold CCP.
thermoview_only: Does NOT write 0x0960 (GVSP config; 32-bit block ID default)
Delivers 64,542 GVSP image frames / 236 blocks (Mono16 + YUV422_8 alternating) on camera:35530 -> PC:50554
halcon_only: Sends 'stream_keep_alive' proprietary keep-alive to camera SCSP0

gvsp_stream_evidence.keep_alive_direction: PC:64797 -> camera:<SCSP0> (camera's current stream source port)
gvsp_stream_evidence.negotiation_probe_payload: proprietary; '00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 f0 47 0a 00 f0 47 0a 00 ...' not a GVSP header
gvsp_stream_evidence.scsp0_correlation: keep-alive destination ports equal SCSP0 readback values (36696, 0xA372=41842, 0xB5E1=46561, 0x95AD=38317, ...) - proves keep-alives target the camera's live stream port

interpretation.summary: HALCON opened the camera (node map reads, CCP held), wrote dual-mode register 0x10a110=2 (ACK success), and then entered a ~14-cycle start/stop loop trying to get the stream up. The camera never sent a single GVSP image packet. This pcap is therefore NOT evidence that HALCON can receive interleaved IR/VL data; it is evidence that HALCON ACTIVATES dual mode on the wire but receives nothing.
interpretation.why_no_data: Candidate causes (a) HALCON never writes provider config 0x20a134/0x20a138/0x20a148 that ThermoView uses; (b) 64-bit block ID (0x0960=0x40000000) may not be accepted by the camera's dual-source path despite the ACK; (c) missing SCPD0/heartbeat writes; (d) camera's interleaved engine requires the exact ThermoView write order. All unverified; next experiment list above.
interpretation.correction_to_earlier_doc: tv46l-halcon-dual-mode.md said HALCON's provider resets 0x10a110 to 0 and cannot write it. This capture shows HALCON ITSELF writing 0x10a110=2 successfully (frame 1109/1110). The conclusion 'HALCON cannot receive the dual stream' still holds - but for a different reason: the camera never streams to HALCON even when the register is set by HALCON.
